summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining patching, sparse autoencoders, and large language models for eliciting and interpreting latent or unexpressed knowledge. Existing approaches struggle with complex reasoning tasks, and mechanistic interpretability tools have primarily been used to understand model behavior rather than to extract hidden knowledge. By combining sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching, the framework identifies knowledge-bearing representations within large language models, verifies them through causal probing, and surfaces hidden knowledge without modifying model weights.

target_user.text: The target users are software engineering teams, security practitioners, and AI researchers working with enterprise software and transformer-based large language models, as derived from company patent assignees and automated software security repositories.

jtbd.text: When deploying large language models in complex reasoning and security tasks, developers want to reliably extract and interpret latent knowledge without altering model weights, so that they can surface hidden information and verify model behavior accurately.

value_prop.text: The combination bridges mechanistic interpretability and latent knowledge elicitation by locating knowledge-bearing representations and applying representation engineering to surface hidden knowledge. This achieves high elicitation accuracy and outperforms standard contrastive consistency search and direct linear probing.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption, driven by axis D score 2.0, is that enterprise users will actively demand and adopt a specialized latent knowledge elicitation tool rather than relying on standard prompting or fine-tuning techniques.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption on desirability, set up a demand landing page explaining the latent knowledge extraction framework and conduct structured problem interviews with enterprise AI developers and security teams.
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: Success is measured by a proposed threshold of 30 percent conversion on the landing page sign-up form and qualitative validation from at least 10 problem interviews confirming an urgent need for weight-free latent knowledge extraction.

kill_criteria.text: The opportunity should be killed if fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of landing page visitors register interest or if interviewees report that weight-based fine-tuning completely fulfills their requirement for uncovering hidden knowledge.

open_source.use: Leverages automated interpretability to help language models understand their own internal sparse autoencoder representations.
Measures internal model state changes and unlearning depth using activation patching techniques.
Provides automated benchmarking for LLM agents on real-world software security tasks.

to_build.text: A unified interface layer that couples sparse autoencoder feature extraction pipelines with real-time activation patching engines for seamless latent knowledge elicitation.
